answer: Agents can require each account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can place orders, then slash that stake when a bonded challenge proves the account duplicated an identity or manipulated trades. A challenge succeeds only with evidence checked against public transaction history, so rivals cannot simply accuse competitors at will. The stake makes each extra persona costly: a sybil operator must tie up more capital and risks losing it, while a ripple of coordinated fake bids can expose links across accounts. Even saffron sellers in an ocean-sized market face that cost.
